methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops targeting the technology gap in Hampton Roads represent peer-to-peer knowledge transfer that could build distributed, grassroots capability outside traditional tech hubs—a critical signal of whether deep skills can spread beyond NoVA.

signals.title: ‘Shaping our future’: Company powering AI data centers invests $50+ million in Henrico, adding 200 jobs - WWBT
signals.signal_reading: A $50M+ investment in AI data center infrastructure in Henrico with 200 jobs reinforces Richmond's emergence as a secondary concentration point, but signals capital-intensive rather than distributed capability—deepening metro advantages while leaving rural regions behind.

signals.title: Norfolk could get AI assist for non-emergency calls - WAVY.com
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk's adoption of AI for non-emergency dispatch represents shallow, platform-delivered AI implementation in public services—broad adoption without deep technical capability building, typical of vendor-driven digital transformation.

signals.title: Virginia Beach schools bring ChatGPT under division oversight as AI use grows - 13newsnow.com
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Beach schools bringing ChatGPT under division oversight signals widespread but shallow AI adoption—users consuming platform tools rather than building deep AI literacy, potentially widening the gap between tool users and tool creators.

signals.title: Southwest Field Notes: National Black Lung Association to meet next week in Abingdon amid historic high numbers of the disease in central Appalachia
signals.signal_reading: A public hearing on data centers in Scott County amid black lung discussions highlights Southwest Virginia's struggle with infrastructure-heavy AI economy impacts while lacking the workforce development or broadband foundation to capture AI opportunity—infrastructure without capability access.
